One purpose of the Kernel Arena is to exhibit alternative kernel implementations, both variants of established ones and new ones, and to see if they can withstand the onslaught of clever people trying to break them.

But so far this has not happend that much, so maybe this ecosystem needs a little bootstrapping push… so here we go :)

The mini-kernel is a small naive implementation of a Lean typechecker. It does not support everything yet (no mutual or nested inductives, no reduction of string literals), but so far I believe it is sound, i.e. you cannot prove False with it.

I even intentionally made some bold design choices so that there is actually a good chance that the kernel is incomplete.

So here is the bounty: If you are first to prove False with it (by way of a correctly structured proof export file), I’ll send you a Lean t-shirt.

The kernel arena has infrastructure to somewhat conveniently construct bad proof terms from Lean surface syntax, see the tutorial tests, but a hand-written .ndjson file is also valid. Preferred form of submission of a new test case at https://github.com/leanprover/lean-kernel-arena.

Of course, breaking the other checkers is also interesting and helpful. In particular I’d be curious if @Paul Reichert ’s sonanoda idea is sound.
Can we grandfather in a shirt for @Tristan Stérin?

EDIT: This is not a soundness bug, see the actual bug below.

Aristotle claimed to have found a real soundness bug this time.

{"thm": {"name": 3, "levelParams": [], "type": 2, "value": 3, "all": [3]}}
The bug is that we can define Nat to be False, but inferType (line 207 in the mini-kernel) always returns "Nat" for .natLit, so we can produce a value of type False using .natLit 0.

I think the mini-kernel's parseExprStrLit function is wrong since in the Lean 4 export format, strVal is a string, not an object. It should instead be

def parseExprStrLit (json : Json) : M Expr := do
  let .str strVal := json | fail s!"Expr.lit strVal invalid"
  return .strLit strVal

After making this change, the same soundness bug works for strings and .strLit too.

Ah, I should have clarified that “invalid prelude definitions” doesn't count - that's known and accepted, and is the same for the official kernel, and comparator has provisions against that.

I'm looking for exploits that would pass comparator with a challenge of theorem unsoundness : False := sorry.

The bug is in Level.isNotZero, which incorrectly returns true on the input .param 0. So we can create a universe-polymorphic inductive MyBool.{u} : Sort u | tt | ff where the recursor MyBool.rec.{1,0} can do large elimination of a Prop.
But because of proof irrelevance we have tt = ff, so we can derive a contradiction.

Good catch! I guess I first have to hand t-shirts out for all the stupid bugs before people will attack the stupid but more interesting design decisions :)

That’s worth a kernel tutorial test case! I’ll have to think about how to produce that using the tutorial infrastructure… :thinking:

Ok, fixed and added as a test case to the arena (will show up in a few hours when it has built).

This was useful, so I’ll put up a second t-shift for the next one!
Just a reminder that this bounty is still available. And I’m also accepting soundness issue reports about nanobruijn (a fork of nanoda with a differen term and binder representation)
